Her visible facial impression is guided by the supplied photograph, expressed through rounded dark eyes, softly shaped brows, a small nose and naturally glossy lips. A brief warm glance toward the camera interrupts her concentrated work. She wears a butter-yellow cotton dress with short sleeves rolled for the task; its ordinary folds follow her stance at the bench. Her left hand steadies the press edge while her right hand lays the damp paper into the open press. Both forearms stay below the visible ponytail root, keeping her work and the hairstyle legible together. Her hairstyle forms one readable arrangement on her head. Dark chestnut scalp hair converges smoothly to a single low fastening base immediately behind her right ear. One continuous loose ponytail emerges from this base, travels over her right shoulder and ends at her upper chest. A narrow three-strand scalp braid begins at her visible right temple, with its first crossing just behind the outer end of her right eyebrow. It follows the side of her head above the right ear. At least three alternating strand crossings are distinct along this temple-to-ear route. Its final crossings run along the visible outer side of the hair above and behind the upper ear rim, then slope into the upper front edge of that same low ponytail base. The whole last braided segment and its entry into the gather remain exposed on the camera-facing side, making the braid-to-root connection traceable from one crossing to the next. A deep cobalt cloth ribbon wraps this one fastening root and closes in a compact knot, two bow loops and two short ends. Immediately above the cobalt wrap, a small polished silver crescent barrette grips the gathered hair. Its lower edge meets the hair directly beside the upper edge of the wrap, and a narrow contact shadow separates rigid silver from the strands. The barrette, cloth wrap and braid terminal are neighboring parts of the same visible root assembly, while their separate materials remain readable. Rain beads cling to the glass panes; a shallow catch tray and recovered, slightly wavy herbarium papers on the bench make the recent leak and the rescue work understandable. Green leaves beyond the glass and the worn wooden press surround her without competing with the hair structure. Clear late-afternoon light after rain reveals strand crossings, cloth folds, silver edges and naturally textured skin. Photograph the scene from her front-right, about 65 degrees around toward her right side and 18 degrees above eye level. Keep environmental portrait framing, her whole head through below her waist, the entire tail and both working hands, with enough depth of field for the right temple, ear-side braid, fastening root and press to remain readable. The photograph carries a quiet, warm pause in purposeful work.

definitions.principle: These creative definitions guide agent-owned choices within requester meaning, not clinical classifications. Zero/off disables added treatment, never removes explicitly requested content or artistic judgment. Expression levels describe prominence in the whole image; creativity levels describe interpretive freedom. Neither measures exposure percentages, detail quotas, quality scores, or native image-model parameters. Intensity and expression are separate choices; higher intensity does not prescribe a garment, material or expression category. Creativity leaves style, extra props and surreal treatment open to the request and artistic judgment. Emphasis directs only active sensual and fetish axes without changing their intensities. Popular permits familiar appeal without requiring trend search; overt is an available expression, not the mandatory meaning of level three. Choose a coherent expression suited to this particular scene. Sensual and fetish may share the same expressive choice.
